session_covered: US and European sessions of Tuesday 13 October
intro: Covers the US session of Tuesday 13 October. This brief was generated about 20 minutes before the US cash close (07:00 AEDT), so US figures are late-session snapshots, not final closes. FNArena was unreachable; figures are from alternative sources.
footnotes: S&P 500: approximate figure (the email gave "~7,805 pts (intraday) -0.03%").
NASDAQ Composite: approximate figure (the email gave "~27,215 pts (intraday) -0.1%").
Dow Jones Industrial Average: approximate figure (the email gave "~51,680 pts (intraday) -0.3%").
US 10-year Treasury yield: approximate figure (the email gave "~5.22% -2 bp").
Brent crude: the email gave "~US$104.4–105.2/bbl -1.3% to -2.1%", which isn't a single figure, so it isn't shown in full.

US index figures are intraday snapshots (about 12:30–15:00 ET) versus Monday closes (S&P 7,807.24; Nasdaq 27,245.90; Dow 51,850.55); Dow snapshots ranged from -0.16% to -0.3%. VIX and 10-year yield confirmed by two sources. Brent differs by source (AP early session US$105.22, -1.3%; TheStreet US$104.40, -2.1%). Gold is a spot/CFD reference; an early gold futures snapshot showed US$4,210 (+0.47%). AUD/USD is single-source (Trading Economics). The iron ore print is dated 12 October; 13 October not available.
Futures sources disagreed (TradingView 8,786, +0.42%; Investing.com 8,745.5, +0.78%), so the implied open is the midpoint of the 8,821-8,852 range.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures (Dec 2026 contract) are up on both sources but disagree on level: TradingView 8,786 (+0.42%); Investing.com 8,745.5 (+67.5, +0.78%). Reported as up roughly 0.4–0.8%, level 8,745–8,786, low confidence (timestamps unclear; US still trading). Applied to the prior ASX 200 close of about 8,784 (essentially flat, -0.01%, Tuesday), the implied open is about 8,821–8,852, i.e. +37 to +68 points (+0.4% to +0.8%).

local_events: No scheduled Australian data release or RBA event could be verified for 14 October.
The RBA lifted the cash rate to 4.6% earlier this month; the next meeting is 2–3 November.
what_moved: A global chip selloff (reports that China's CXMT advanced a memory chip design, plus AI-valuation worries) weighed on the Nasdaq, while the Dow was supported by bank and health care earnings and gains in Meta and Salesforce. Treasury yields eased slightly from multi-year highs and oil fell. S&P 500 sector percentages: not available. Korea's Kospi fell about 5.5% and Japan's Nikkei 1.8%; most other Asian and European indexes edged higher.

news.headline: Chip stocks slide worldwide.
news.summary: Micron fell 5.8%, AMD 3.3% and Nvidia and Broadcom about 1.3% in early trade.

news.headline: US bank earnings season opens.
news.summary: Goldman Sachs beat, JPMorgan missed on profit but lifted its net interest income outlook, and Wells Fargo missed. Dimon flagged elevated asset prices, inflation and rate risks.

news.headline: Treasury yields near multi-year highs.
news.summary: The 10-year eased to about 5.20–5.22% from 5.24%; softer jobs and inflation data have reduced bets on near-term hikes.

news.headline: Oil falls.
news.summary: The US temporarily eased restrictions on Russian diesel supply; uncertainty over possible US action on Iran persists.

news.headline: ASX 200 ends flat.
news.summary: Banks rose and miners fell; NAB business confidence was at a four-month low in September.

news.headline: RBA tightening weighs on households.
news.summary: The cash rate rose to 4.6%; Westpac consumer sentiment fell 4.7% to 80.4 in October and Westpac expects another hike in November.

coming_up: US September CPI, Wednesday 14 October 08:30 ET (23:30 AEDT tonight); consensus headline 3.7% y/y, core 2.5%. US PPI follows Thursday 15 October. (Source: Charles Schwab)
